All right, I've just kicked off the background tasks to download the Three.js core library and the OrbitControls module into the `lib` directory. Those downloads are still in progress, so I can't reference those files in any code yet. However, the texture assets have already been fetched successfully into `textures`, and the directory structure (`js`, `css`) is already in place. The next logical step is to lay down the HTML scaffold that will load the CSS, the JavaScript modules, and set up the basic UI elements (loading screen, header, sidebars, HUD, etc.) for the digital twin.

I need to create an `index.html` file at the root of the project (`D:\physics\earth\index.html`). This file should:
- Declare a proper HTML5 doctype and language.
- Include meta tags for charset and viewport.
- Set a descriptive `<title>`.
- Link to the stylesheet that will live in `css/style.css`.
- Provide an import map so that the ES module loader can resolve the `three` import to the local `lib/three.module.js` and the OrbitControls import to `lib/OrbitControls.js`. Using an import map keeps the `<script type="module">` in `js/main.js` clean and avoids hard‑coding CDN URLs.
- Add a `<canvas id="scene">` that the Three.js renderer will target.
- Insert a loading overlay (`#loading`) with a spinner, status text, and progress bar. This will be hidden once the textures and scene are ready.
- Build the top navigation bar (`#topbar`) containing the brand header, a simulation clock with time‑control buttons, and a search box for location lookup.
- Add a side panel (`#layers`) with checkboxes for toggling various visual layers (clouds, atmosphere, night lights, stars, graticule, ISS, auto‑rotate). These correspond to the features I plan to implement in `main.js`.
- Include a HUD (`#hud`) that will display live cursor coordinates, altitude, sub‑solar point, and ISS status.
- Provide an info panel (`#info-panel`) that can be shown when a user clicks a location, with a close button and placeholders for title, coordinates, and extra info.
- Add a footer with attribution for the NASA imagery and a brief usage hint.
- Finally, load the main JavaScript module (`js/main.js`) as a `<script type="module">`.

All of these elements are static HTML; they don't depend on the library files being present yet, but they do reference them via the import map, which will resolve correctly once the background download finishes. I should ensure the file paths are correct: CSS at `css/style.css`, JS modules under `js/`, and libraries under `lib/`. The import map syntax must be valid JSON inside a `<script type="importmap">`.

Now I just need to write the content to `index.html`. I'll construct the HTML string exactly as I described, preserving indentation and line breaks for readability. Then I will issue a `Write` tool call with `file_path` set to `D:\\physics\\earth\\index.html` and `content` set to the full HTML document.

This will lay the foundation for the rest of the project, allowing me to later populate `css/style.css`, `js/main.js`, and hook up the interactive features. Proceeding with the write.
